causes.change: The change under test: source, workflow or configuration in the pushed commit.
causes.transient: Transient infrastructure. Re-run the failed jobs, or the next push retries.
causes.operator: An owner or operator must act; re-running alone will not fix it.
causes.unknown: The code alone does not decide it; start at the reported check or stage.

uncatalogued.title: Uncatalogued failure code
uncatalogued.meaning: The step reported a code that the failure catalogue does not describe, so no explanation is available.
uncatalogued.next: Add the code to ci_outcomes.json (staging_cd_outcome_tests.py should have required it), then read the step's source at the reported check.

staging_cd_build.py: Build context does not exclude required credential paths
Dockerfile differs from the shared deployables registry
Native image must use its expected unprivileged numeric user
staging_cd_contract.py: Runtime compatibility declaration has duplicate fields
AM requirements and runtime image declarations disagree

refused.title: Input check refused
refused.meaning: A fixed check in this step refused its input, a remote read or a precondition; the condition is the require or Refusal at the reported line.
refused.next: Open the reported line at this commit: its message states the failed condition. Fix the input it names, or re-run if it rejects a remote read.

timeout.title: Step timed out
timeout.meaning: A command or remote call exceeded its time bound.
timeout.next: Re-run the failed jobs. If it repeats, the reported line shows which bound to investigate.

network.title: Network connection failed
network.meaning: A connection to a remote service failed before it answered.
network.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check the service used at the reported line.

http-server.title: Remote service unavailable
http-server.meaning: A remote service answered with a server error or asked the client to slow down.
http-server.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check the service's status.

http-denied.title: Remote access denied
http-denied.meaning: A remote service refused the job's credential with HTTP 401 or 403.
http-denied.next: Check the token or credential used at the reported line and its permissions.

http-client.title: Remote request refused
http-client.meaning: A remote service refused the request with an HTTP client error, for example because the resource is absent.
http-client.next: Check what the reported line requests; a re-run alone rarely helps.

os-error.title: System call failed
os-error.meaning: A file or process operation failed; its error text is withheld because it can contain sensitive data.
os-error.next: Check the file or process used at the reported line; re-run if it depends on runner state.

error.title: Unexpected error
error.meaning: The step raised an exception that no check anticipated, which usually means malformed input or a script defect.
error.next: Reproduce the step from the reported line with the same inputs, then fix the script or the input and add a test.

declined.title: Step did not confirm success
declined.meaning: The step finished without raising but did not confirm success, for example because a child process failed or the command is unknown.
declined.next: Check that the workflow passes a supported command; if the step runs a child process, re-run, then reproduce that child locally.

registry_denied.title: Registry access denied
registry_denied.meaning: The container registry rejected the publisher credential with HTTP 401 or 403.
registry_denied.next: Confirm the workflow token may write packages and the package grants this repository write access, then re-run the failed jobs.

build_failed.title: Image build failed
build_failed.meaning: The image build exited unsuccessfully; its output is withheld because it can contain sensitive data.
build_failed.next: Build the component's Dockerfile locally at the reserved commit to see the error, fix it and push.

command_failed.title: Image tool failed
command_failed.meaning: An image or registry command other than the build exited unsuccessfully.
command_failed.next: Re-run the failed jobs. If it repeats at the same stage, run that stage's tool locally against the built image.

build_timeout.title: Image build timed out
build_timeout.meaning: The image build exceeded its one-hour bound.
build_timeout.next: Re-run the failed jobs. If builds keep growing, check the cache restore and the slowest build layers.

command_timeout.title: Image tool timed out
command_timeout.meaning: An image or registry command exceeded its time bound.
command_timeout.next: Re-run the failed jobs; repeated timeouts at the same stage point to registry or runner capacity.

scan_refused.title: Image scan refused
scan_refused.meaning: The layer scan found content or packages the image policy forbids. OS package layers can change without a source change when a build applies the latest upstream security updates.
scan_refused.next: Read SCAN_EVIDENCE: findings in OS package layers need the image owner's reviewed classification of the new upstream content; remove findings this change added to the image, then push.

registry_read_failed.title: Registry read failed
registry_read_failed.meaning: A registry read returned an error other than access denied.
registry_read_failed.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check the registry's availability and the tag this stage reads.

validation_refused.title: Input check refused
validation_refused.meaning: A fixed check refused the release input; its condition is the require or Refusal at the reported line.
validation_refused.next: Open the reported line at this commit: its message states the failed condition. Fix the input it names, or re-run if it rejects a remote read.

io_failed.title: File or process error
io_failed.meaning: A local file, directory or process operation failed on the runner.
io_failed.next: Check the file or path used at the reported line; re-run if it depends on runner disk space.

unexpected_error.title: Unexpected error
unexpected_error.meaning: An exception outside the publication vocabulary stopped the stage.
unexpected_error.next: Reproduce the stage from the reported line, then fix the script or its input and add a test.

reservation_owner_mismatch.title: Reservation owned by another attempt
reservation_owner_mismatch.meaning: The version reservation belongs to a different run attempt, which happens when only the publish job is re-run.
reservation_owner_mismatch.next: Re-run all jobs of the workflow run, or push again, so allocation reserves a version for the new attempt.

reservation_superseded.title: Reservation superseded
reservation_superseded.meaning: A newer develop source took this component's version reservation, so this publication stopped.
reservation_superseded.next: No action: the newer run publishes this component.

registry_digest_conflict.title: Registry tag holds another digest
registry_digest_conflict.meaning: The reserved registry tag holds a digest other than the scanned archive, so this publication refused to claim it.
registry_digest_conflict.next: An operator inspects who wrote the reserved tag before any retry; tags are never overwritten.

registry_write_uncertain.title: Registry copy outcome uncertain
registry_write_uncertain.meaning: The copy to the registry failed in transport and its tag could not be read back to settle the outcome.
registry_write_uncertain.next: Read the reserved tag in the registry: if it holds the scanned digest the copy landed; otherwise push again for a new version.

registry_not_visible.title: Pushed image not visible yet
registry_not_visible.meaning: The image copy finished, but reading its tag or digest back kept returning 404 for the whole settle window (about 45 s). The registry had not yet served the write at the edge that answered.
registry_not_visible.next: Re-run the failed jobs; the reserved version is read back again before anything is rewritten. If it repeats, check GitHub Packages status and that the tag exists in the package.

runtime_cleanup_incomplete.title: Runtime canary cleanup incomplete
runtime_cleanup_incomplete.meaning: The runtime canary's Docker containers, volume or local image could not be proven removed after two cleanup passes; nothing was published.
runtime_cleanup_incomplete.next: Re-run the release; runtime-cleanup.json names the smoke result and failed cleanup step. failure=identity_refused means the runner held containers or a volume this run did not create: inspect its Docker inventory, do not re-run.

validate.title: Validate inputs
validate.meaning: checks the publication tasks, the reservation and the source identity.
validate.next: Compare the publication task and reservation with this run's allocation output.

resume.title: Resume a published receipt
resume.meaning: confirms that an already published digest still exists before reusing it.
resume.next: Re-run; if the digest is gone, the version must be published again from a new push.

snapshot.title: Snapshot the reserved source
snapshot.meaning: exports the reserved source commit into a clean build directory.
snapshot.next: Re-run; check that the reserved commit is still reachable from develop.

reuse.title: Reuse a qualified archive
reuse.meaning: looks for an already qualified image archive with identical inputs.
reuse.next: Re-run; reuse is an optimisation and a miss falls back to a build.

build.title: Build the image
build.meaning: builds the component image from the reserved source.
build.next: Build the same Dockerfile locally at the reserved commit.

registry_preflight.title: Check the registry slot
registry_preflight.meaning: confirms that the reserved version tag is still absent from the registry.
registry_preflight.next: If the tag already exists, it was published outside this pipeline and an operator must reconcile it.

inspect.title: Inspect the image
inspect.meaning: checks the built image's labels, platform and identity.
inspect.next: Compare the image labels with the release identity that the reported check expects.

scan.title: Scan image layers
scan.meaning: scans every layer for secrets and checks packages against the image policy.
scan.next: Read SCAN_EVIDENCE: get upstream OS package content reviewed by the image owner, or remove content this change added.

runtime_smoke.title: Runtime smoke test
runtime_smoke.meaning: starts the runtime image in a canary and checks that it boots.
runtime_smoke.next: Run the runtime image locally and check its startup.

archive_check.title: Check archive integrity
archive_check.meaning: confirms that the image archive did not change between scan and push.
archive_check.next: Re-run; a repeated change points to runner disk corruption.

registry_login.title: Log in to the registry
registry_login.meaning: authenticates the publisher to the registry.
registry_login.next: Check the workflow token's package permissions.

registry_copy.title: Push the image
registry_copy.meaning: copies the exact scanned archive to the registry.
registry_copy.next: Re-run; check the registry's status if it repeats.

registry_verify.title: Verify the pushed digest
registry_verify.meaning: reads back the pushed tag and checks its digest.
registry_verify.next: Re-run; a lasting mismatch needs an operator to inspect the registry tag.

receipt.title: Write the receipt
receipt.meaning: records the published receipt for finalization.
receipt.next: Check the receipt field that the reported line validates.

cache_restore.title: Restore the build cache
cache_restore.meaning: restores the Cargo cache bundle before the build.
cache_restore.next: Re-run; a cold cache only slows the build.

cache_export.title: Export the build cache
cache_export.meaning: saves the Cargo cache bundle after a successful publication.
cache_export.next: A re-run is optional: the image is already published.

artifact_unavailable.title: Receipt artifact unavailable
artifact_unavailable.meaning: The publish job's receipt artifact is missing, oversized or not a regular file.
artifact_unavailable.next: Re-run all jobs so publication uploads the receipt again.

recovery_oid_unverified.title: Earlier final tag differs
recovery_oid_unverified.meaning: A final tag from an earlier attempt does not match the object this attempt expected.
recovery_oid_unverified.next: An operator must compare the final tag with the published receipt before any retry.

attempt_burned.title: Version burned by a failed attempt
attempt_burned.meaning: An earlier attempt pushed this version without finalizing it, so the version cannot be reused.
attempt_burned.next: Push again or re-run all jobs: allocation reserves a new version.

receipt_order_invalid.title: Receipts reordered or duplicated
receipt_order_invalid.meaning: The published receipts do not match the publication tasks one to one.
receipt_order_invalid.next: Compare the publish job's receipts with its tasks; a mismatch indicates a script defect.

resume_mismatch.title: Resumed receipt changed
resume_mismatch.meaning: A resumed receipt differs from the receipt recorded for its task.
resume_mismatch.next: An operator must reconcile the published version before retrying.

allocation_mismatch.title: Receipt differs from its allocation
allocation_mismatch.meaning: The published identity differs from the reservation that allocation owns.
allocation_mismatch.next: Compare the receipt with this run's allocation output, then re-run all jobs.

digest_unverified.title: Published digest unverified
digest_unverified.meaning: The registry does not show the published digest.
digest_unverified.next: Re-run; if the digest stays missing, publish again from a new push.

final_conflict.title: Final version conflict
final_conflict.meaning: A different immutable final release already exists for this source or tag.
final_conflict.next: An operator must inspect the existing final tag; final tags are never overwritten.

reservation_missing.title: Reservation missing
reservation_missing.meaning: The version reservation for this publication no longer exists.
reservation_missing.next: Check whether another run finalized or removed the reservation; push again to allocate a new version.

reservation_superseded.title: Reservation superseded
reservation_superseded.meaning: A newer source took over this component's reservation.
reservation_superseded.next: No action: the newer run finalizes this component.

annotation_failed.title: Final tag object not created
annotation_failed.meaning: Git could not create the annotated final tag object.

final_unverified.title: Final tag unverified
final_unverified.meaning: After the push, the final tag could not be read back as expected.
final_unverified.next: Re-run the failed jobs; finalization settles an already pushed tag before it retries.

unexpected_existing_ref.title: Final tag already present
unexpected_existing_ref.meaning: The tag push reported the ref as already up to date instead of newly created.
unexpected_existing_ref.next: An operator must check who created the final tag.

cleanup_final_unverified.title: Cleanup lacks a verified final
cleanup_final_unverified.meaning: The pending reservation cannot be deleted because its matching final tag was not verified.

cleanup_owner_mismatch.title: Pending version owned elsewhere
cleanup_owner_mismatch.meaning: The pending reservation for this version belongs to another source.
cleanup_owner_mismatch.next: An operator must inspect the pending tag before it is deleted.

cleanup_unverified.title: Reservation cleanup unverified
cleanup_unverified.meaning: The pending reservation still exists after its deletion.
cleanup_unverified.next: Re-run the failed jobs; the final tag is already published.

github_read_failed.title: GitHub read failed
github_read_failed.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check GitHub's status and the workflow token's permissions.

history_unverified.title: Develop history unverified
history_unverified.meaning: The develop first-parent history could not be verified.

source_history_invalid.title: Source not on develop
source_history_invalid.meaning: The release source is not on verified develop first-parent history.
source_history_invalid.next: Check develop for a force push or rewritten history; an operator must reconcile it.

registry_read_failed.title: Registry read failed
registry_read_failed.meaning: A registry read returned an error other than access denied.
registry_read_failed.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check the registry's availability and the tag this stage reads.

registry_denied.title: Registry access denied
registry_denied.meaning: The registry rejected the read credential with HTTP 401 or 403.
registry_denied.next: Confirm the workflow token may read packages, then re-run the failed jobs.

validation_refused.title: Input check refused
validation_refused.meaning: A fixed check refused finalization; its condition is the require or Refusal at the reported line.
validation_refused.next: Open the reported line at this commit: its message states the failed condition. Fix the input it names, or re-run if it rejects a remote read.

command_timeout.title: Command timed out
command_timeout.meaning: A git or registry command exceeded its time bound.

io_failed.title: File or process error
io_failed.meaning: A local file, directory or process operation failed on the runner.
io_failed.next: Check the file or path used at the reported line; re-run if it depends on runner disk space.

unexpected_error.title: Unexpected error
unexpected_error.meaning: An exception outside the finalization vocabulary stopped the stage.
unexpected_error.next: Reproduce the stage from the reported line, then fix the script or its input and add a test.

event.title: Check the event
event.meaning: confirms that the run is an authorized develop push.
event.next: Finalization runs only for develop pushes; check the workflow trigger.

artifact.title: Read the receipt artifact
artifact.meaning: reads the publish job's receipt artifact.

attempt.title: Check earlier attempts
attempt.meaning: checks receipts produced by earlier attempts of this run.
attempt.next: Compare earlier-attempt receipts with the final tags.

receipt.title: Validate receipts
receipt.next: Check the receipt field named at the reported line.

allocation.title: Match the allocation
allocation.meaning: matches each receipt to its allocated reservation.
allocation.next: Compare the receipts with this run's allocation output.

registry_verify.title: Verify the registry digest
registry_verify.meaning: confirms that the published digest exists in the registry.

final_read.title: Read final tags
final_read.meaning: reads the component's existing final tags.

reservation_read.title: Read the reservation
reservation_read.meaning: confirms that the reservation is still current.

tag_create.title: Create the final tag
tag_create.meaning: creates the annotated final tag object.

tag_push.title: Push the final tag
tag_push.meaning: pushes the final tag and its outcome ref atomically.

final_verify.title: Verify the final tag
final_verify.meaning: reads the pushed final tag back.

cleanup_verify.title: Verify before cleanup
cleanup_verify.meaning: checks the final tag before the pending reservation is deleted.

cleanup_read.title: Confirm the cleanup
cleanup_read.meaning: confirms that the pending reservation is gone.

output.title: Write job outputs
output.meaning: writes the final receipt to the job outputs.
output.next: Check the output value that the reported line validates.

RESERVATION_OWNER_UNREADABLE.title: Reservation owner unreadable
RESERVATION_OWNER_UNREADABLE.meaning: The workflow run that owns an existing reservation could not be read.

RESERVATION_OWNER_INVALID.title: Reservation owner invalid
RESERVATION_OWNER_INVALID.meaning: An existing reservation names a run that is not a develop push of this repository.
RESERVATION_OWNER_INVALID.next: An operator must inspect the pending reservation tag.

RESERVATION_OWNER_UNCERTAIN.title: Reservation owner state uncertain
RESERVATION_OWNER_UNCERTAIN.meaning: The run that owns an existing reservation reported an unexpected status.

RESERVATION_OWNER_INCONSISTENT.title: Reservation run and attempt disagree
RESERVATION_OWNER_INCONSISTENT.meaning: The run that owns a reservation exists, but its recorded attempt does not.
RESERVATION_OWNER_INCONSISTENT.next: An operator must inspect the pending reservation tag.

QUEUE_INVALID.title: Release queue invalid
QUEUE_INVALID.meaning: The plan job's release queue is malformed.
QUEUE_INVALID.next: Check the plan job's output; a malformed queue indicates a planner defect.

CHANGE_INVALID.title: Release change invalid
CHANGE_INVALID.meaning: A queued change has an invalid source, tree or component list.
CHANGE_INVALID.next: Check the plan job's output; an invalid change indicates a planner defect.

FINAL_VERSION_CONFLICT.title: Conflicting final versions
FINAL_VERSION_CONFLICT.meaning: The source already has final versions that disagree with each other.
FINAL_VERSION_CONFLICT.next: An operator must reconcile the final tags for this source.

MERGED_PR_NOT_UNIQUE.title: Merged pull request not unique
MERGED_PR_NOT_UNIQUE.meaning: The source does not belong to exactly one merged develop pull request.
MERGED_PR_NOT_UNIQUE.next: Land changes on develop only through one merged pull request per commit.

MERGED_PR_IDENTITY_CHANGED.title: Merged pull request changed
MERGED_PR_IDENTITY_CHANGED.meaning: The pull request associated with the source changed between reads.

VERSION_LABEL_REQUIRED.title: Conflicting or unsupported version labels
VERSION_LABEL_REQUIRED.meaning: The merged pull request carries multiple version-upgrade labels or an unsupported version-upgrade label.
VERSION_LABEL_REQUIRED.next: Keep one supported version-upgrade label or remove all version-upgrade labels to use patch, then re-run the failed jobs.

VERSION_LABELS_INVALID.title: Version labels malformed
VERSION_LABELS_INVALID.meaning: The pull request's labels could not be read as names.

SOURCE_HISTORY_INVALID.title: Source not on develop
SOURCE_HISTORY_INVALID.meaning: The release source is not on verified develop first-parent history.
SOURCE_HISTORY_INVALID.next: Check develop for a force push or rewritten history; an operator must reconcile it.

GITHUB_READ_FAILED.title: GitHub read failed
GITHUB_READ_FAILED.meaning: A GitHub API read failed without a transient or permission cause: another HTTP status, an oversized response, or a gh failure whose diagnostic names no network fault.
GITHUB_READ_FAILED.next: Open the reported line; if it repeats, compare the read with the GitHub API and the workflow token's permissions.

GITHUB_READ_TRANSIENT.title: GitHub read unavailable
GITHUB_READ_TRANSIENT.meaning: GitHub API reads kept failing transiently: a 5xx, 408 or 429 response, a rate-limited 403, or no response at all.
GITHUB_READ_TRANSIENT.next: Re-run the failed jobs; if it repeats, check GitHub's status.

GITHUB_READ_DENIED.title: GitHub read denied
GITHUB_READ_DENIED.meaning: GitHub answered an API read with 401, or 403 without rate-limit headers. The workflow fixes the token's permissions, so a 403 that comes and goes is usually a secondary rate limit, not a permission change.
GITHUB_READ_DENIED.next: If this read passed in recent runs, re-run the failed jobs. Otherwise an operator must check the allocate job's token permissions (contents, pull-requests, actions) and the Actions settings.

GITHUB_RESPONSE_INVALID.title: GitHub response invalid
GITHUB_RESPONSE_INVALID.meaning: A GitHub API response did not have the expected shape.
GITHUB_RESPONSE_INVALID.next: Re-run the failed jobs; a repeat suggests the API response changed.

RESERVATION_COLLISION_LIMIT.title: Too many reservation collisions
RESERVATION_COLLISION_LIMIT.meaning: Concurrent runs repeatedly took the planned version slot.
RESERVATION_COLLISION_LIMIT.next: Re-run the failed jobs after the concurrent runs finish.

RESERVATION_PUSH_FAILED.title: Reservation push failed
RESERVATION_PUSH_FAILED.meaning: Pushing the reservation tag failed without a collision.

RESERVATION_PUSH_REJECTED.title: Reservation push rejected
RESERVATION_PUSH_REJECTED.meaning: GitHub declined the atomic reservation push and none of its refs exist: the token may not write tags, or a tag ruleset or hook refused them.
RESERVATION_PUSH_REJECTED.next: An operator must check the allocate job's contents permission and the rulesets and hooks that cover cma- tags, then re-run the failed jobs.

RESERVATION_VERIFY_FAILED.title: Reservation not verified
RESERVATION_VERIFY_FAILED.meaning: The pushed reservation could not be read back as this run's claim.

FINAL_SETTLEMENT_UNCERTAIN.title: Final settlement uncertain
FINAL_SETTLEMENT_UNCERTAIN.meaning: A terminal reservation could not be settled against its final receipt.

FINAL_SETTLEMENT_CONFLICT.title: Final settlement conflict
FINAL_SETTLEMENT_CONFLICT.meaning: A terminal reservation differs from its final receipt.
FINAL_SETTLEMENT_CONFLICT.next: An operator must reconcile the reservation with the final tag.

DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.title: Allocation deadline exceeded
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.meaning: An allocation attempt, or a GitHub read within it, ran out of its 120 second budget.

READ_FAILED.title: Allocation read failed
READ_FAILED.meaning: A reservation or tag read failed.

WRITE_UNCERTAIN.title: Allocation write uncertain
WRITE_UNCERTAIN.meaning: A reservation write timed out and may already have committed.
WRITE_UNCERTAIN.next: Re-run the failed jobs; allocation settles the earlier write first.

INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE.title: Tag inventory incomplete
INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE.meaning: The version tag inventory could not be read completely.

DEVELOP_ADVERTISEMENT_UNSETTLED.title: Advertised develop history does not settle the push
DEVELOP_ADVERTISEMENT_UNSETTLED.meaning: The live ref and its available first-parent history did not establish that this push is current or superseded.
DEVELOP_ADVERTISEMENT_UNSETTLED.next: Re-run the failed jobs after develop's ref and history agree with the push.

INVENTORY_CLAIM_CONFLICT.title: Claim and reservation differ
INVENTORY_CLAIM_CONFLICT.meaning: A version claim and the pending reservation of its version name different objects in one tag advertisement, so the inventory is damaged and every read repeats it.
INVENTORY_CLAIM_CONFLICT.next: An operator must compare the cma-allocation claim with the pending tag of that version and restore the pair one run wrote.

INVENTORY_CLAIM_ORPHANED.title: Claim listed without a version
INVENTORY_CLAIM_ORPHANED.meaning: A version claim was listed without its pending reservation or its final tag. One listing is not an atomic snapshot, so another job's push or finalization can show this for a moment; allocation reads the inventory again once in the job.
INVENTORY_CLAIM_ORPHANED.next: Re-run the failed jobs. If it persists after the re-run, a pending or final tag was deleted, and an operator must restore it for that claim.

INVENTORY_TOO_LARGE.title: Tag inventory too large
INVENTORY_TOO_LARGE.meaning: The repository's tag advertisement exceeds the 16 MiB that allocation reads, and grows with every release.
INVENTORY_TOO_LARGE.next: An operator must prune obsolete tags, or raise the bound in staging_cd_allocation_snapshot.py in its own change.

RESERVATION_COLLISION.title: Reservation collision
RESERVATION_COLLISION.meaning: Another run claimed the planned version slot first.
RESERVATION_COLLISION.next: Re-run the failed jobs; the next allocation plans a new version.

RESERVATION_PLAN_INVALID.title: Reservation plan invalid
RESERVATION_PLAN_INVALID.meaning: Planning produced a reservation for a retired component, or for a version the inventory or this plan already holds; an allocator defect, not a race.
RESERVATION_PLAN_INVALID.next: Reproduce allocation from the reported line, fix the planner and add a test; a re-run plans the same reservation.

RESERVATION_NOT_VISIBLE.title: Reservation not yet visible
RESERVATION_NOT_VISIBLE.meaning: The pushed reservation was not yet visible when read back.

UNEXPECTED_ERROR.title: Unexpected error
UNEXPECTED_ERROR.meaning: An exception outside the allocation vocabulary stopped allocation.
UNEXPECTED_ERROR.next: Reproduce allocation from the reported line, then fix the script or its input and add a test.

UNCLASSIFIED_REFUSAL.title: Unclassified refusal
UNCLASSIFIED_REFUSAL.meaning: A fixed check refused allocation with a message outside the allocation vocabulary; its condition is at the reported line.
UNCLASSIFIED_REFUSAL.next: Open the reported line to read the condition. If it recurs, add its message to REFUSAL_CODES in staging_cd_allocate.py and to this catalogue.

publication-unqualified.title: Publication unqualified
publication-unqualified.meaning: The component's published receipt failed verification or is not finalized.
publication-unqualified.next: Open the component's Release job: its FAIL publication or FAIL finalize line explains why.

publication-read-failed.title: Publication read failed
publication-read-failed.meaning: Reading the component's published receipt or registry state failed.

superseded-source.title: Superseded source
superseded-source.meaning: A newer develop source has already published this component.
superseded-source.next: No action: the newer run deploys this component.

contract-group-incomplete.title: Contract group incomplete
contract-group-incomplete.meaning: AM and runtime images that share a contract change must deploy together, and a member is missing.
contract-group-incomplete.next: Fix the failed Release job of the missing member; the group deploys once every member qualifies.

contract-group-mismatch.title: Contract group mismatch
contract-group-mismatch.meaning: The AM and runtime images do not share a compatible contract.
contract-group-mismatch.next: Land the AM and runtime sides of a contract change together, then push.

contract-analysis-unavailable.title: Contract analysis unavailable
contract-analysis-unavailable.meaning: The compatibility of the AM and runtime contract could not be evaluated.

deploy-precondition.title: Deployment not admitted
deploy-precondition.effect: Nothing. The deployment controller was not started.

mode.title: Deployment mode invalid
mode.meaning: The mode is not release or bootstrap, an automatic run asked for bootstrap, or bootstrap lacked a component.
mode.next: Check the dispatch inputs or the workflow's deployment mode, then dispatch again.

checkout.title: Infrastructure checkout invalid
checkout.meaning: The infrastructure checkout is absent, differs from the resolved commit or links its entry point.
checkout.next: An operator must check the infrastructure revision resolved for this run.

policy.title: Deployment policy unreadable
policy.meaning: The deployment policy could not be read or is invalid.
policy.next: An operator must check the deployment policy.

credentials-format.title: Deployment credentials malformed
credentials-format.meaning: The deployment credentials are missing, empty or contain whitespace.
credentials-format.next: An operator must check the deployment client credential secrets.

budget.title: Admission budget expired
budget.meaning: Deployment started too long after admission: the budget is 120 seconds for a release and 45 for bootstrap.
budget.next: Re-run the deployment; persistent expiry means runner queueing exceeds the budget.

authority.title: Deployment authority refused
authority.meaning: The release set was superseded, would split the contract group, or could not be written for the controller.
authority.next: Usually a newer push supersedes this one and no action is needed; otherwise re-run the deployment.

input.title: Deployment input invalid
input.meaning: The release set, event or environment failed validation before the controller started.
input.next: Open the reported line to see which input failed validation.

deploy-private.title: Deployment refused
deploy-private.effect: Nothing. The deployment controller refused before any mutation.

permit.title: Deployment permit refused
permit.meaning: The deployment controller did not grant this run a deployment permit.
permit.next: An operator must check the deployment permit for this repository.

authentication.title: Deployment authentication failed
authentication.meaning: The deployment service rejected the deployment credential.
authentication.next: An operator must rotate or restore the deployment client credentials.

authorization.title: Deployment authorization refused
authorization.meaning: The deployment credential lacks permission for this deployment.
authorization.next: An operator must grant the deployment client its required permission.

clock.title: Controller time budget refused
clock.meaning: The controller stopped before any change because a time budget ran out: the admission was too old when it started, or a pre-change check (preflight) used its whole budget.
clock.next: Re-run the deployment. If it repeats, check whether a component it depends on, such as the Agent Manager, was restarting or unready at the time.

inventory.title: Deployment inventory unreadable
inventory.meaning: The controller could not read or validate the current deployment inventory.
inventory.next: Re-run the deployment; if it repeats, an operator must check the staging deployment state.

compatibility.title: Compatibility unverified
compatibility.meaning: The controller's compatibility checks failed, which includes reading or promoting the runtime compatibility state.
compatibility.next: Re-run the deployment; if it repeats, an operator checks the runtime promotion and compatibility state.

image-version.title: Image version refused
image-version.meaning: The controller refused the image version, for example because it is not newer than the deployed one.
image-version.next: No action while a newer release deploys; otherwise compare the released and deployed versions.

image-identity.title: Image identity unverified
image-identity.meaning: The controller could not verify the image's identity, which includes failing to read it from the registry.
image-identity.next: Re-run the deployment; if it repeats, an operator checks registry access and the image's identity labels.

baseline.title: Deployed baseline differs
baseline.meaning: The deployed baseline differs from what the controller expected.
baseline.next: An operator must reconcile the staging deployment with its recorded state.

readiness.title: Target not ready
readiness.meaning: The staging target was not ready to accept a deployment.
readiness.next: Re-run the deployment after the current rollout settles.

apply-abandoned.title: Stored generation never applied
apply-abandoned.meaning: chrono-cd stored a new generation of one of the staging apps this release depends on or deploys but never applied it: it stays pending with no reconcile result long after any apply ends. No rollout is running, so a re-run refuses again.
apply-abandoned.next: An operator finds the app left pending, runs the deployment service's admin reconcile for that app (see the cma-infra staging README) or re-submits the same spec, waits for ready, then re-runs.

transport.title: Deployment service unreachable
transport.meaning: The controller could not reach the deployment service.

acceptance.title: Acceptance precondition refused
acceptance.next: An operator must check the acceptance prerequisites in the controller log.

schema.title: Request schema refused
schema.meaning: The controller does not support this release request's schema.
schema.next: Align the deployment controller and this repository on one release request schema.

fence.title: Deployment fence held
fence.meaning: Another deployment holds the staging fence.
fence.next: Re-run after the other deployment finishes.

configuration.title: Controller configuration refused
configuration.meaning: The controller's reviewed configuration, deployment budgets, web overlays or the secret bindings the spec requires failed validation.
configuration.next: An operator must check the deployment controller's configuration for this component.

publication.title: Publication evidence refused
publication.meaning: The controller refused the release's publication evidence: its receipt, signal, publisher or scan policy.
publication.next: Check the component's Release job and its publication receipt; if they are valid, an operator checks the controller's publication policy.

internal-error.title: Controller internal error
internal-error.meaning: The controller refused its own malformed call or raised an unexpected error. This is a controller defect, not a property of the release.
internal-error.next: An operator must give this run's deployment controller log to the controller's owner.

interrupted.title: Controller interrupted
interrupted.meaning: The controller was interrupted before it changed anything.

preflight.title: Preflight refused
preflight.next: An operator must check the controller's preflight requirements in its log.

unreported.title: Refusal reason unreported
unreported.meaning: The controller refused before any mutation but reported no reason.
unreported.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log for this run.

unrecognized.title: Refusal reason unrecognized
unrecognized.meaning: The controller reported a refusal reason that this repository does not know; the token is withheld.
unrecognized.next: Add the controller's new reason to REASONS in staging_cd_refusal.py and to this catalogue.

am-replicas.title: Agent Manager scaled beyond the release budget
am-replicas.meaning: Agent Manager runs more replicas than the production release budget is sized for (2). A rollout at that count could outlast the deployment window, so the controller refused before any write.
am-replicas.next: Wait until Agent Manager scales back to its steady-state count, then re-run the deployment. Nothing was changed.

deploy-verification.title: Deployment unverified
deploy-verification.effect: Staging may have changed and its state is unproven. An operator must reconcile it before staging is trusted again.

write-timeout.title: Deployment write timed out
write-timeout.meaning: Applying the deployment did not complete within its bound.
write-timeout.next: Check the deployment service's status; re-run once staging is reconciled.

write-response.title: Deployment write rejected
write-response.meaning: The deployment service returned an unexpected response to the change.
write-response.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log for the response.

read-timeout.title: Status read timed out
read-timeout.meaning: Reading the deployment status did not complete within its bound.

read-response.title: Status read invalid
read-response.meaning: The deployment status response was invalid.
read-response.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log for the response.

status-reconcile.title: Status not reconciled
status-reconcile.meaning: The deployment service did not report the new state as reconciled.

status-counts.title: Replica counts differ
status-counts.meaning: Ready or updated replica counts did not reach their expected values.
status-counts.next: Check the released components' staging pods for failing readiness probes; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

status-inventory.title: Deployed inventory differs
status-inventory.meaning: The deployed resources differ from the release inventory.
status-inventory.next: An operator must check for resources changed outside this pipeline.

status-pods.title: Pods not ready
status-pods.meaning: Pods of the new release were not running and ready.
status-pods.next: Check the released components' staging pod events and logs; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

pod-restarts.title: Pods restarted
pod-restarts.meaning: New release pods restarted during verification, usually from a crash or failing liveness probe. A runtime or runtime-omarchy release only reconfigures the Agent Manager, so its restarted pods are Agent Manager pods.
pod-restarts.next: Check the restarted pods' logs (Agent Manager's for a runtime release). "native warm pool startup readiness failed" means the new runtime's warm pool was not ready in time, not a broken image; if this change caused it, fix it.

pod-restarts-membership.title: Agent Manager restarted after losing authority
pod-restarts-membership.meaning: Agent Manager reported lost membership or ownership before the restart.
pod-restarts-membership.next: Use the previous Agent Manager container log to investigate membership or ownership renewal.

pod-restarts-startup-gate.title: Agent Manager restarted at the warm-pool startup gate
pod-restarts-startup-gate.meaning: The active runtime pool did not reach startup readiness before the Agent Manager stopped.
pod-restarts-startup-gate.next: Check active warm-pool readiness, provider capacity and quota for the Sandbox namespace.

pod-restarts-panic.title: A release container restarted after a panic
pod-restarts-panic.meaning: The previous container log recorded a panic before the restart.
pod-restarts-panic.next: Open the restarted container's previous log and inspect the panic.

rollout-ownership.title: Rollout ownership unproven
rollout-ownership.meaning: The rollout could not be attributed to this deployment.
rollout-ownership.next: An operator must check for a concurrent manual or second deployment.

rollout-timeout.title: Rollout timed out
rollout-timeout.meaning: The rollout did not complete within its budget.
rollout-timeout.next: Check the released components' staging pods for slow startup or readiness; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

rollout-failed.title: Rollout failed
rollout-failed.meaning: The deployment service reported the rollout as failed.
rollout-failed.next: Check the released components' staging pod events; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

image-digest.title: Running digest differs
image-digest.meaning: Running pods do not use the released image digest.
image-digest.next: An operator must check for a concurrent deployment or an image override.

ownership.title: Resource ownership differs
ownership.meaning: The deployed resources are not owned by this pipeline.
ownership.next: An operator must check who changed the staging resources.

recovery-ownership.title: Recovery ownership unproven
recovery-ownership.meaning: The rollback could not prove that it owns the resources it restored.
recovery-ownership.next: An operator must reconcile staging manually.

recovery-revision.title: Recovery revision unproven
recovery-revision.meaning: The rollback could not restore or prove the previous revision.
recovery-revision.next: An operator must restore the previous release manually.

phase-budget.title: Controller time budget exceeded
phase-budget.meaning: The controller ran past its time budget, so its result cannot be trusted.
phase-budget.next: An operator must confirm the staging state; then re-run the deployment.

image-identity.title: Image identity differs
image-identity.meaning: The running image's identity labels differ from the release.
image-identity.next: An operator must check for a concurrent deployment or an image override.

served-identity.title: Served identity differs
served-identity.meaning: The running service reports a different build identity from the release.
served-identity.next: Check that the component serves this release's build identity and that no older pod still answers.

status-shape.title: Status shape invalid
status-shape.meaning: The deployment status document had an unexpected shape.
status-shape.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log.

pod-evidence.title: Pod evidence missing
pod-evidence.meaning: Evidence about the new pods could not be collected or validated.

cohort.title: Serving cohort unproven
cohort.meaning: The serving AM and runtime cohort could not be proven compatible.
cohort.next: An operator must confirm which AM and runtime versions serve staging.

serving.title: Service not serving
serving.meaning: The new release did not serve requests successfully.
serving.next: Check the released components' health endpoints and logs in staging; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

acceptance.title: Acceptance check failed
acceptance.next: Reproduce the acceptance check against this release; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

startup-observation.title: Startup not observed
startup-observation.meaning: The controller could not observe the new release starting.
startup-observation.next: Check the released components' staging pod logs for startup errors.

startup-schema.title: Startup evidence invalid
startup-schema.meaning: The startup evidence did not match its expected schema.
startup-schema.next: Check that the component's startup output still matches the expected schema.

namespace-fence.title: Namespace fence unconfirmed
namespace-fence.meaning: The staging namespace fence could not be confirmed.
namespace-fence.next: An operator must check the staging namespace fence.

interrupted.title: Controller interrupted
interrupted.meaning: The controller was interrupted, for example by cancellation or a runner shutdown.
interrupted.next: An operator must confirm the staging state; then re-run the deployment.

result.title: Controller result invalid
result.meaning: The controller's component result was missing or failed validation.
result.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log for this run.

permit.title: Deployment permit refused
permit.meaning: After staging changed, the deployment permit or the reviewed mode policy refused a later step.
permit.next: An operator must check the deployment permit for this repository.

authentication.title: Deployment authentication failed
authentication.meaning: After staging changed, the deployment service rejected the deployment credential.
authentication.next: An operator must rotate or restore the deployment client credentials.

authorization.title: Deployment authorization refused
authorization.meaning: After staging changed, the deployment credential lacked permission for a later step.
authorization.next: An operator must grant the deployment client its required permission.

clock.title: Controller clock refused
clock.meaning: After staging changed, the controller's timing check refused to continue.

inventory.title: Deployment inventory unreadable
inventory.meaning: After staging changed, the controller could not read or validate the deployment inventory.
inventory.next: Re-run once staging is reconciled; if it repeats, an operator must check the staging deployment state.

compatibility.title: Compatibility unverified
compatibility.meaning: After staging changed, the runtime compatibility state could not be read, validated or promoted.
compatibility.next: An operator checks the runtime promotion and compatibility state; then re-run.

image-version.title: Image version refused
image-version.meaning: After staging changed, the controller refused the released or deployed image version.
image-version.next: Compare the released and deployed versions in the controller log.

baseline.title: Baseline unproven
baseline.meaning: The previous release or the rollback baseline could not be read or proved.
baseline.next: An operator must reconcile the staging deployment with its recorded state.

readiness.title: Target not ready
readiness.meaning: A readiness check outside the named rollout and pod checks failed, such as the Event Gateway's readiness or startup logs.
readiness.next: Check the released components' staging pods and startup logs; if this change caused it, fix it and push.

apply-abandoned.title: Stored generation never applied
apply-abandoned.meaning: chrono-cd stored this deployment's new generation of an app but never applied it: the app stays pending with no reconcile result long after any apply ends, so staging may still run the earlier spec.
apply-abandoned.next: Run the deployment service's admin reconcile for the app left pending (see the cma-infra staging README) or re-submit the same spec. That applies this run's unverified write, so then re-run this deployment so it is verified.

transport.title: Deployment service unreachable
transport.meaning: The controller could not reach the deployment service or a public endpoint, including after its retries.

schema.title: Document schema refused
schema.meaning: A release request, app spec, live view or schema-state document failed its closed schema or the reviewed spec policy.
schema.next: Read the controller log for the refused document; a release that requires a migration needs the reviewed migration first.

fence.title: Deployment fence changed
fence.meaning: Resource ownership or the recorded preimage changed during the deployment, or the write would change more than the owned image.
fence.next: An operator must check for a concurrent manual or second deployment.

configuration.title: Controller configuration refused
configuration.meaning: The controller's reviewed configuration, deployment budgets, web overlays or the secret bindings the spec requires failed validation.
configuration.next: An operator must check the deployment controller's configuration for this component.

publication.title: Publication evidence refused
publication.meaning: The controller refused the release's publication evidence: its receipt, signal, publisher or scan policy.
publication.next: Check the component's Release job and its publication receipt; if they are valid, an operator checks the controller's publication policy.

internal-error.title: Controller internal error
internal-error.meaning: The controller refused its own malformed call or raised an unexpected error. This is a controller defect, not a property of the release.
internal-error.next: An operator must give this run's deployment controller log to the controller's owner.

unreported.title: Reason unreported
unreported.meaning: The controller reported no reason for this check.
unreported.next: An operator must read the deployment controller's log for this run.

unrecognized.title: Reason unrecognized
unrecognized.meaning: The controller reported a reason that this repository does not know; the token is withheld.
unrecognized.next: Add the controller's new reason to VERIFICATION_REASONS in staging_cd_refusal.py and to this catalogue.

am-replicas.title: Agent Manager scaled beyond the release budget
am-replicas.meaning: Agent Manager ran more replicas than the production release budget is sized for (2), so the rollout could not be proven inside its window.
am-replicas.next: An operator confirms the deployment state, waits until Agent Manager scales back to its steady-state count, then re-runs the deployment.

deploy-verification.next: An operator reconciles staging first. Then: {next}

deploy-release.title: Release rolled back
deploy-release.effect: Staging changed, the release failed this check, and the controller restored and verified the previous release.

deployed-compatibility-unqualified.title: Withheld: compatibility unqualified
deployed-compatibility-unqualified.meaning: The component was withheld because it is not proven compatible with the AM and runtime versions deployed in staging.
deployed-compatibility-unqualified.next: Release the AM and runtime sides of the contract together so the group can be proven compatible.

deployment-unverified.title: Deployment unverified
deployment-unverified.meaning: The controller could not verify this component's deployment.
deployment-unverified.next: An operator must reconcile the component in staging.

deploy-controller.title: Deployment input refused
deploy-controller.effect: Not reported here. The controller exits 40 for an input or configuration error, normally before it changes anything; an operator confirms in its log.

input-error.title: Controller input or configuration error
input-error.meaning: The deployment controller rejected this release's input or its own configuration.
input-error.next: An operator reads the deployment controller's log for this run and fixes the input or configuration it names.

deploy-contract.title: Contract group withheld
deploy-contract.effect: AM and runtime components were not deployed; independent components could still proceed.

contract-read-failed.title: Configured contract digests unreadable
contract-read-failed.meaning: The AM and runtime digests configured in staging could not be read, so the contract group was withheld.
contract-read-failed.next: Re-run the deployment; if it repeats, an operator checks that the deployment controller can read the staging configuration.

deploy-clock.effect: Nothing. Deployment setup did not start.

admission-time.title: Admission time invalid or expired
admission-time.meaning: The admission timestamp is missing, malformed, in the future, or older than the budget of 120 seconds for a release and 45 for bootstrap.
admission-time.next: Re-run the deployment; persistent expiry means runner queueing exceeds the admission budget.

invalid-public-evidence.title: Component result invalid
invalid-public-evidence.meaning: The deploy job's component result failed validation against the admitted release set.
invalid-public-evidence.next: Compare the deploy job's component_result output with the admitted release set; an operator must confirm the staging state.

evidence-invalid.title: Outcome evidence invalid
evidence-invalid.meaning: The job results or component failures could not be validated, so no deployment acceptance is claimed.
evidence-invalid.next: Check the admission and deployment jobs of this run, then re-run the redeployment.

deployment-not-accepted.title: Deployment not accepted
deployment-not-accepted.meaning: The deployment job failed, was cancelled, or was skipped although a release set was expected.
deployment-not-accepted.next: Open the Deploy set job: its FAIL line names the precondition, verification or release reason.

publication-failed.title: Publication or qualification failed
publication-failed.meaning: One or more components failed publication or qualification.
publication-failed.next: Read each FAIL component line of this step: its reason names the next step.

allocation-incomplete.title: Allocation incomplete
allocation-incomplete.meaning: Allocation did not succeed, so no component deployment is proven.
allocation-incomplete.next: Open the allocate job: its FAIL allocation line names the code and the next step.

evidence-invalid.title: Outcome evidence invalid
evidence-invalid.meaning: The component outcome evidence is missing or invalid, so no deployment is proven.
evidence-invalid.next: Check the Release and Promote jobs of this run for a failure that left no outputs.

publish-failure.title: Publication failed
publish-failure.meaning: The component's publication or finalization job failed.
publish-failure.next: Open the component's Release job: its FAIL publication or FAIL finalize line names the stage, reason and check.

publish-cancelled.title: Publication cancelled
publish-cancelled.meaning: The component's publication was cancelled, usually by a newer push or by hand.
publish-cancelled.next: No action if a newer push is running; otherwise re-run the failed jobs.

publish-skipped.title: Publication skipped
publish-skipped.meaning: Publication did not run, usually because an earlier job of this run failed.
publish-skipped.next: Fix the first failed job of this run.

publish-unknown.title: Publication result unknown
publish-unknown.meaning: No publication result was recorded for the component.
publish-unknown.next: Check whether the component's Release job was scheduled in this run.

finalize-incomplete.title: Finalization incomplete
finalize-incomplete.meaning: The component published but its final version tag was not confirmed.
finalize-incomplete.next: Open the component's Finalize job: its FAIL finalize line names the stage and reason.

reservation_superseded.title: Reservation superseded
reservation_superseded.meaning: A newer run took over this component's reservation, so this run intentionally skipped its release.
reservation_superseded.next: No action: the newer run publishes and deploys this component.

source_already_final.title: Source already finalized
source_already_final.meaning: An older run already finalized this source, so this run skipped its group claim before building and no run is known to deploy it.
source_already_final.next: An older run finalized this source; the next develop push resumes this group's final; push to deploy (a re-run allocates nothing once develop moves on).

superseded_by_newer_final.title: Deployment owned by a newer final
superseded_by_newer_final.meaning: A newer final from a later develop source exists for this component, so this run deployed nothing for it.
superseded_by_newer_final.next: No action: the newer final's run deploys this component.

superseded-peer.title: Held with a skipped member
superseded-peer.meaning: The component published and finalized, but its lane was not deployed because another member's publication was skipped.
superseded-peer.next: Follow the skipped member's row: it names the run or the push that deploys this lane.

admit-skipped.title: Admission skipped
admit-skipped.meaning: The admission job did not run for this component.
admit-skipped.next: Fix the first failed job of this run.

admit-unknown.title: Admission unreported
admit-unknown.meaning: The admission job ran but reported no decision for this component.
admit-unknown.next: Open the component's Admit job and check its outputs.

deploy-failure.title: Deployment failed
deploy-failure.next: Open the Deploy job: its FAIL line names the precondition, verification or release reason.

deploy-cancelled.title: Deployment cancelled
deploy-cancelled.next: No action if a newer push is deploying; otherwise an operator must confirm the staging state and re-run.

deploy-skipped.title: Deployment skipped
deploy-skipped.meaning: The deployment job did not run, usually because admission or infrastructure resolution failed.
deploy-skipped.next: Fix the first failed job of this run.

deploy-unknown.title: Deployment result unknown
deploy-unknown.meaning: No deployment result was recorded for the component.
deploy-unknown.next: Check whether the Deploy job was scheduled in this run.

controller-unreported.title: Controller outcome unreported
controller-unreported.meaning: The deployment finished without a verified controller outcome for this component.
controller-unreported.next: Open the Deploy job: its FAIL line and summary state what the controller proved.

retry-not-run.title: Automatic deployment retry did not run
retry-not-run.meaning: The first deployment was refused before any change for a transient reason and handed over to one automatic re-admission and retry, but that retry never started or never reported. Nothing is deployed for this component in this run.
retry-not-run.next: Open the lane's Re-admit and Deploy again jobs. If they were cancelled or skipped, dispatch redeploy-staging for the component or push to develop; a re-run of failed jobs reuses an expired admission.

oversize-compressed.title: Cache bundle too large
oversize-compressed.meaning: The compressed Cargo cache bundle exceeds its bound, so it was not saved.
oversize-compressed.next: Reduce cached build output, or raise the bound in staging_cd_cargo_artifact.py after review.

oversize-expanded.title: Expanded cache too large
oversize-expanded.meaning: The expanded Cargo cache exceeds its bound, so it was not saved.
oversize-expanded.next: Reduce cached build output, or raise the bound in staging_cd_cargo_artifact.py after review.

empty.title: Cache mount empty
empty.meaning: A Cargo cache mount was empty after the build, so nothing was saved.
empty.next: Check that the build still uses its Cargo cache mounts.

transfer-failed.title: Cache transfer failed
transfer-failed.meaning: Exporting the cache mounts from the builder failed or timed out.
transfer-failed.next: No action: the next build restores the previous bundle.

invalid.title: Cache export invalid
invalid.next: Check the cache exporter in staging_cd_build_cache.py.

release-plan.title: Release plan incomplete
release-plan.effect: Nothing. No image was published or deployed by this run.

incomplete.title: Selection budget exhausted
incomplete.meaning: The selection cache did not cover the plan window, usually after a selector policy change, and analysing the rest exceeded the plan's budget. Analysed revisions were saved; INCOMPLETE gives the count.
incomplete.next: Catch-up re-runs this once from its hourly check, continuing from the saved revisions. To shorten a wide window, set CMA_CD_ADOPTION_SHA to a later develop merge; it raises the start.

finals-unreadable.title: Lane releases unreadable
finals-unreadable.meaning: The tag listing or a lane's newest final release tag could not be read after repeated attempts within the plan's read budget. Nothing was planned.
finals-unreadable.next: Catch-up re-runs this once from its hourly check after the outage settles; the next develop push plans again too.

finals-untrusted.title: Lane release tag untrusted
finals-untrusted.meaning: A lane's newest final release tag, or the tag listing, failed the checks allocation also applies, or GitHub serves no tag object for it. Nothing was planned.
finals-untrusted.next: Inspect the tags of the lanes the PLAN refused line names; allocation would refuse the same tag.

floor-required.title: Adoption floor required
floor-required.meaning: A lane's newest final is not on the last 2,000 develop first-parent merges, so its window needs CMA_CD_ADOPTION_SHA on that history.
floor-required.next: Set CMA_CD_ADOPTION_SHA to a recent develop merge after which the lanes the PLAN refused line names need nothing older.

anchor-unselected.title: Contract transition unselected
anchor-unselected.meaning: The selector did not select the AM/runtime group at the older contract transition the window keeps, so the group's coupling cannot be planned.
anchor-unselected.next: Review the selector change: a contract transition must select its group. The PLAN refused line names the merge.

finals-denied.title: Lane release read refused
finals-denied.meaning: GitHub rejected the plan step's credential (401) while reading a lane's newest final release tag, or the step has no token. Nothing was planned.
finals-denied.next: Check that the plan step receives GH_TOKEN and that it can read this repository's contents; the PLAN refused line names the lanes.

manifest-boundary.title: Window crosses a lane addition
manifest-boundary.meaning: The window reaches the merge that added a lane to the deployable manifest. The selector cannot compare across it, because the parent's manifest lacks that lane.
manifest-boundary.next: Set CMA_CD_ADOPTION_SHA to a develop merge after the one the PLAN refused line names (at=); nothing before it can be compared.

scan-review.title: Scanner bundle not accepted
scan-review.effect: Nothing. No image was built, published or deployed by this run.

unreviewed.title: Scanner bundle not reviewed by the controller
unreviewed.meaning: This checkout scans with a bundle (the SCAN-REVIEW line names it) that the pinned deployment controller does not list in REVIEWED_SCANS, so every deployment would be refused.
unreviewed.next: Merge the infrastructure repository's REVIEWED_SCANS entry for this bundle after its independent review, then re-run this workflow.

unreadable.title: Controller scan policy unreadable
unreadable.meaning: The deployment controller's reviewed scanner set could not be read or parsed at the pinned infrastructure revision.
unreadable.next: Re-run the workflow; if it repeats, check the infrastructure reader token and the controller's reviewed_scan.py declaration.
